currentContext.business: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Limited is a global pharmaceutical company headquartered in Hyderabad, India, whose portfolio spans active pharmaceutical ingredients, generic formulations including biosimilars, OTC products, innovative products and custom pharmaceutical services. It concentrates on therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Central Nervous System, Pain Management, Gastro-Intestinal and Cardiovascular, and serves major markets including the USA, India, Russia & CIS, China, Brazil and Europe. The business reports along two lines - Global Generics, which now also carries an acquired Nicotine Replacement Therapy consumer healthcare portfolio, and Pharmaceutical Services and Active Ingredients (PSAI).

currentContext.expansion: Dr. Reddy's expansion in FY2026, as described in the routed sections, is portfolio-, filing- and geography-led rather than a named greenfield capex programme: no plant, line, commissioning date, capacity figure or capex outlay is disclosed here. The largest capacity- and reach-adding move of the year is the acquired Consumer Healthcare business in Nicotine Replacement Therapy ('NRT'), which the Board credits with augmenting Global Generics growth and which was the primary driver of the Europe business alongside new generic product launches - an acquisition that extends the Company's consumer-health franchise and route to market across Europe. The second expansion vector is US regulatory pipeline and capability build-out: during the year the Company filed 15 Abbreviated New Drug Applications ('ANDAs') in the United States, and as of March 31, 2026 there were 77 generic filings awaiting approval with the US Food and Drug Administration, comprising 75 ANDAs and two New Drug Applications filed under Section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act - a filed-but-unapproved block that represents the next tranche of US market entry. The third is scale-up of the Pharmaceutical Services and Active Ingredients (PSAI) platform, where the Company filed 128 Drug Master Files (DMFs) worldwide including 16 filings in the US, and attributes growth to new launches of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient products and to momentum in the pharmaceutical services business. Geographic expansion appears as new launches across Emerging Markets supported by higher volumes, and new brand launches in India including the innovation portfolio. The corporate overview frames the footprint this build-out serves: a portfolio spanning APIs, generic formulations including biosimilars, OTC products, innovative products and custom pharmaceutical services, focused on Oncology, Central Nervous System, Pain Management, Gastro-Intestinal and Cardiovascular, sold into the USA, India, Russia & CIS, China, Brazil and Europe.

risks.risk: Concentration on a small number of high-value US products
risks.note: North America revenues declined year-on-year 'largely on account of lower revenues from lenalidomide', showing that the erosion of a single limited-competition product can swing the Company's largest geography.
European growth was 'partially offset by price erosion in generics' - a structural feature of the regulated generic markets the Company serves, which caps realisation even when volumes grow.

risks.risk: API price pressure in the PSAI business
risks.note: PSAI growth was 'offset by lower API prices', so new API launches and services momentum can be neutralised by realisation decline.
As of March 31, 2026 there were 77 generic filings awaiting approval with the USFDA (75 ANDAs and two 505(b)(2) NDAs); the timing of new-product revenue is gated by an external regulator.
The Company reported no forced recalls but 17 voluntary recalls during the year; recalls in a regulated pharmaceutical supply chain carry both revenue and reputational consequences.

Growth in Global Generics, Emerging Markets, India, Europe and PSAI was each described as supported by 'favourable foreign exchange rate movements', and 68% of standalone product turnover is sold outside India - the same channel can reverse.

risks.risk: Talent retention in an R&D- and quality-dependent organisation
risks.note: Permanent employee turnover was 19.7% in FY2025-26 across a 27,527-strong permanent employee base, a continuing retention burden for a business whose output depends on scientific and quality talent.
2,128 customer complaints were filed during FY2025-26 under the BRSR grievance disclosure, a scale of consumer interaction that must be managed to avoid regulatory and reputational escalation.

one-line thesis: Base business grew double-digit excluding Lenalidomide, with India and Emerging Markets driving resilience; key pipeline milestones achieved (Semaglutide India approval, Abatacept BLA filed) but biosimilar launches delayed by regulatory setbacks, while one-off Labour Code provision distorted margins — what matters is the sustainability of India’s 17-18% organic growth and execution on Semaglutide’s global rollout.

guidance: revenue growth: base business double-digit; margin: 25% EBITDA margin target (ex-one-offs); order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: no explicit FY27 capex guidance, Q3 capex ₹669cr ($75M)
segment / subsidiary detail: North America Generics: -16% YoY (Lenalidomide decline); Europe Generics: +4% YoY; Emerging Markets: +32% YoY (₹1,896cr); India: +19% YoY (17-18% organic, Stugeron contribution); PSAI: -5% YoY; NRT: +25% YoY (8% constant currency)
growth verticals / optionality: Semaglutide: 87+ markets via COPP, India launch March 2026, Canada May 2026 (goal date), Brazil/Turkey July 2026; Abatacept: IV BLA filed Dec 2025, US approval expected end CY2026, EU July 2026 submission; Denosumab/Rituximab: CRL delays, EU launched, US pending; Eftilagimod Alfa: strategic collaboration for oncology in key ex-US/EU/Japan markets

capex / expansion: Q3FY26: ₹669cr ($75M); no FY27 guidance provided; focus on capacity for Semaglutide (12M pens currently, expandable), biosimilars, and API facilities
capital allocation: Net cash surplus ₹3,069cr ($342M); BD activity: $20M upfront + $350M milestones for Eftilagimod Alfa; no dividend or buyback mentioned; prioritizing pipeline investment and selective BD over share buybacks
risks & watch-items: USFDA CRLs on Denosumab and Rituximab biosimilars; regulatory delays in Canada/US for Semaglutide; pricing pressure in US/EU generics; Lenalidomide cliff impact; currency volatility; execution risk on NRT integration and Abatacept commercialization
management quality / tone: Confident on base business growth (India, EM), optimistic on Semaglutide pipeline, pragmatic on biosimilar delays; transparent on Labour Code provision; cautious on pricing competition; tone is execution-focused, not defensive
non-obvious takeaways: Labour Code provision is retrospective (not prospective), impacting P&L but not recurring at same scale; Semaglutide API is synthetic (same as Novo), countering Health Canada’s substitutability skepticism; NRT profitability >25% EBITDA margin, exceeding original model; APSL contributed to 2 of 46 FDA-approved novel drugs in 2025

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.
